title: Micro Objectives Sprint Scratch - Eli Schneider
content:
Sprint scratchpad (two-week micro-objectives) - purpose: keep a tiny, iterated personal OKR that is easy to track mid-sprint and can be converted into a short retro. Raw, unfiltered notes.

Top objective (sprint): carve 8 focused hours to ship the batching experiment prototype and validate cost delta on small-chat workload.
Why this matters: shipping a small experiment faster reduces uncertainty for Optimize team recommendations and gives concrete metrics for next planning. Also helps unblock Maya's eval harness dependency.

Key results (two-week targets):
- KR1: Merge a functional prototype PR + basic perf numbers (P50/P95 latency and per-token cost) documented in PR description. Target: PR merged by day 10.
- KR2: Validate cost delta >= 12% on representative small-chat trace (run on dedicated dev pool). Save CSV and add to INF-1023.
- KR3: Run 3 manual QC prompts and record any quality regressions (if >2 regressions escalate to rollback checklist).
- KR4: Protect 8 deep-work hours: aim for 4 focus blocks (90m each) and 2 smaller blocks (45m).

Weekly checkpoints (quick):
- Day 1: outline experiment steps, wireframe config flags, open branch.
- Day 3: basic implementation + unit tests for batching scheduler.
- Day 5: first run on dev cluster, note perf + errors.
- Day 8: iterate on kernel selection heuristics.
- Day 10: PR ready + lightweight runbook for QA.

Personal metrics tracker (sprint):
- Focus blocks completed: 3/6 (currently behind, need to reduce meeting load)
- PRs created: 1 (branch: es/batching-small-chat)
- PRs merged: 0
- Incidents pages called in: 0
- Meetings: 5 (too many syncs; cut one recurring meeting next week)
- Passive learning: 2 articles read (quantization notes + scheduler paper)

Open questions / hypotheses to test:
- H1: A hybrid KV caching + micro-batching approach will reduce token compute by ~10–15% for small chat. Need to instrument true per-token GPU time.
- H2: Kernel selection heuristics that prefer grouped shorter sequences will improve batch utilization without hurting P95 more than 8%.
- Q: If we hit quality regressions, do we fallback to conservative kernel selection or to a longer-sequence model variant? (Decision: add a toggle, implement conservative fallback first.)

Risks / friction:
- Dev pool noisy at peak — might need to run overnight and account for cold caches.
- Maya's eval harness depends on export format; sync with Maya before running full validation (blocked until INF-1023 comment resolved).
- Potential flaky unit tests around KV cache eviction; add deterministic seeds.

Mini action list (short, actionable):
- [ ] Draft PR description template with perf table (include P50/P95/cost per token). (Eli)
- [ ] Add instrumentation hook to measure GPU-ns per token in runtime. (Eli + infra) -> link to INF-1023
- [ ] Ping Maya for eval harness export spec (Slack thread). (Eli)
- [ ] Schedule 2x 90m focus blocks on calendar next Tue/Thu morning (block meetings). (Eli)
- [ ] Add rollback checklist to PR (what to revert, who to notify). (Eli)

Retrospective prompts (for end of sprint):
- What slowed me down most? (meetings, flaky infra, unclear test expectations).
- Which experiment assumptions were wrong? (kernel perf, cache warm-up time).
- What small change could have saved 2–4 hours? (better infra booking, preemptive test stubbing).
- Who should I loop in earlier next time? (Maya, platform QE)

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep commits small and named for perf checkpoint (e.g., perf-check-1, perf-check-2). Makes bisecting easier.
- If perf numbers are noisy, run 10 repeats and use median.
- Use dedicated dev pool between 3–6am for quieter runs if quota allows.

Ideas / experiments to park (backlog):
- Add adaptive batching TTL per-client for chat sessions with low token counts.
- Try light quantization on key layers + monitor hallucination rates.
- Build a small dashboard slice in Ops Console for per-route token costs (quick prototype).

Communication notes (draft snippets):
- Slack update (short): "Working on micro-batching prototype — expect PR by next Tue, will need help running dev pool tests. Main metric: % cost reduction on small-chat."
- PR title template: "es: micro-batching prototype for small-chat — perf numbers + rollback"

Unresolved housekeeping:
- Decide final format for perf CSV column names (agree with Maya and infra).
- Confirm if dedicated dev pool has the new kernel library installed (infra ticket opened).

End-of-day log (quick):
- 2026-03-09: prototype scheduler sketched; unit tests stubbed; focus blocks: 2/6; flagged INF-1023 for instrumentation.

If I return to this mid-sprint, first thing: run the small-chat trace locally with 3 repeats, capture median, and update KR2 progress.
